### 2026-10-18 – # Devlog 3:

**4h**

# Devlog 3:

Today I built the PCB, then I routed everything!

So at first I needed a way to connect the 5 propellers via PWM, so I started googleing. A cheap PWM generator costs about 10$ and a switch from 1 to 5 output pins costs also 10 $...WAY to mouch. So, instead I made my own.

At first, i Research for an hour How I can do it. I thought about using an microcontroller, but that would have been overkill. So, instead I used an Analog Build.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B8T7ewFJxrNAGnjNP1kE2Akpi7xHYXxa/9fdd15d0c439fc9d7d75521722c7685c9f21038a5a7f59495e29857370e6f0f1.png)

At first i tried using USB A, but that cant get me the voltage I need. The fans need about 12V, so Instead I used USB C, as it can go up to 40V (And more using Powerdelivery)

So, that was it.J1 is the USB C mount, U2 is the IC (Integrated circuit) Wich tells the Laptop/PD charger it needs 12V. Then, the U1 is the PWM Generator.

At first, i tried Using an comperator, as an IC wich does it for me (For example the NE555DR) did not exist in my Kicad Data libary( and How hard can it be doing it from scratch??), who will compare a voltage divider To an Seesaw signal to see if The Voltage from the Voltage dividerer (from an Potentiometer) Is bigger than the Seesaw generator. IF so, it would output High and it would have generated an Simple PWM. However, Douring building I found out that generating an Seesaw Signal was not as easy said as done.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B8T7ewFJxrNAGnjNP1kE2Akpi7xHYXxa/7573a7ca99a43e71abf066c8e8a65e6fe64c596bee6cb938f5b62f0e7ad8a979.png)
(Credit to asktheman for the image)

All in all, Building an Seesaw  was complex. However, I found out that an IC existed wich can (more or less) Easily output an Seesaw Signal. And you guess it, it is named NE555DR... So, I got to working finding the files for that, and found a projekt named easyeda2kicad wich easily inports all of that into my Kicad projekt. Well, thanks for that I just did all of the triyng to get it to work with an Seesaw generator and an comperator for the last hour and a half for nothing...

Afhter deciding to go with the NE555DR, I then  Added the 5 output pins for the fans, and then added a Diode so that eventual big voltages/Amperes from the Fans coil can go back to +12V And dont destroy my Mosfet.

Why there is a mosfet, you may ask? I also fought aout just putting the output of the NE555 directply to the input of the Outputs for the fans, but that may be dangerously for the NE555 because the fans may need more power as this IC can offer. So, instead I put the fans directly to +12V, and the output via an MOSFET to ground. A Mosfet is basacly a Switch wich we can toggle via elektronics.

Then, I struggled connecting all of the wires in Kicad (Again)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B8T7ewFJxrNAGnjNP1kE2Akpi7xHYXxa/4297a04934b50436761b4c733589fb955c493ef83d2f7eeddbf2326efbe23e83.png)

But all in all it looks not bad now.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/B8T7ewFJxrNAGnjNP1kE2Akpi7xHYXxa/544239cc2032151c261cc239b7056010ed9466544088a38ccefa2ad5266a72ce.png)

The last thing to do is to add the holder in the 3d Print. Then im done. (I think?)
